text:
Vancouver's losing streak reached five games (0-5-0) in Edmonton, and the Canucks had a hand in how it ended. They had pulled within a goal at 17:25 of the third on Brock Boeser's tip-in, which also gave Filip Hronek his 300th career point on the assist. Then Leon Draisaitl, with Connor McDavid setting him up for the third time in the game, snapped home a 69 percent chance at 19:15 to make it 4-2 for the Oilers.

Edmonton earned it. Our numbers put the Oilers at 3.10 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) against 2.14 for VAN, and gave EDM a 55 percent chance to win if the game were replayed many times. They outshot the Canucks 30-22 and led in every period by chance quality. Draisaitl finished with two goals and an assist on seven shots, and McDavid collected three assists. Devon Levi, a 212th overall pick in 2020 who came up through Northeastern, stopped 20 of 22 and roughly matched what the chances called for, while Leevi Meriläinen allowed three on 29 shots, 0.6 goals worse than expected. The Canucks' goals came on tip-ins, 8 and 9 percent looks, and two of them came late in a period.

The Oilers move on with a home win over a team they have now met three times this season: VAN took the first in overtime, EDM the second in a 9-7 shootout of sorts. For Vancouver, the winless run stretches to five, and the Canucks have now scored twice or more in each of these meetings without banking a win in regulation.
